operations.credit_rule_for_next_section: Only concepts with state USABLE may be assumed in S07. PARTIAL, MENTION_ONLY, MISCONCEPTION_RISK and MISSING receive no automatic prerequisite credit.

effective_campaign_state.note_on_counts: Running local counts only. Mandatory global passes may merge recurring root causes, reject false positives or change severity when later dependency evidence is available.

S07_entry_watchlist: S07 is the first roadmap section allowed to teach the string-method toolkit, Unicode, normalization, casefold and regular expressions. Heavy .strip/.split/.join/.title/.lower/.isdigit use in S05-S06 remains MENTION_ONLY and must not be treated as mastered.

list, dict, set and aliasing may be treated as USABLE from S06. Tuple, slicing, unpacking, shallow/deep copy, nested-structure traversal, sorted(key=), deterministic-output reasoning and missing-value protocols are not fully creditable due S06 defects.
The S06 copy model is unsafe: S07 must not assume that a slice or shallow copy gives independently editable nested data.
The S06 unpacking model is unsafe: successful unpacking proves arity, not semantic field meaning.
Missing vs empty/None remains MISCONCEPTION_RISK because the canonical sentinel helper can collapse states.
Function definition and parameter binding remain PARTIAL from S05; return/docstrings/pure-function idea are USABLE. Do not hide new text concepts inside sophisticated function signatures.
Exceptions/try-except/raise remain MENTION_ONLY until S09 unless curriculum repair explicitly introduces a bounded earlier model.
Lambda, generator expressions, nested comprehensions and variadic *args remain MENTION_ONLY.
JSON remains MENTION_ONLY and is canonically an S08 topic despite S06 scope drift.
Module/import mental model remains MENTION_ONLY until S10; S07 should microdefine any required stdlib imports rather than assume them.
Invariant and O(n) mental models remain risky from earlier sections and cannot be silently assumed.
CP-N1-B/CASO identifiers remain a persistent widow-term family unless expanded globally.
